relevance_note: The paper identifies four LCAT patients individually by genotype, e.g. 'One patient with FED was homozygous for the p.T123I mutation', 'the other compound heterozygous for p.T147I and p.V333M'.
method_note: Case-control biochemical study. Rows only for the 4 homozygous/compound heterozygous patients, labelled 'unnamed person 1-4' in order of first mention in Results (1: FED homozygous p.T147I; 2: FED compound heterozygous p.T147I/p.V333M; 3: FLD homozygous p.C337Y; 4: FLD homozygous p.T345M; the paper's 'either p.C337Y or p.T345M' was read as one FLD patient per variant). The 63 heterozygous carriers are described only as counts and group statistics, with their variants only in an online supplement (Supplementary Table I) not included in this file, so they get no rows; the 63 family controls are relatives not described in relation to a specific person, no rows. Person 1's variant is printed as legacy p.T123I and re-annotated by the authors as p.T147I (HGVS numbering including the 24-aa leader); the HGVS form p.T147I is recorded and the span keeps both. All tables give group means/medians only (sex, age, lipids, CVD 0/4, statin 2/4); none were assigned to individuals; zero counts excluded no one. Phenotype rows come from group statements naming the carriers of 2 defective LCAT alleles (= the four patients). Pathogenicity 'deleterious' comes from the study-design statement naming homozygous and compound heterozygous carriers. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null: references 34-37 are cited for the mutations, not stated to describe these patients. n_patients_reported = 4 + 63 carriers (sum, not printed as one number). No script transcription of tables; JSON assembled by a short script from hand-chosen values.
